Quantum Intelligent Systems: A Hybrid Quantum-Logic Framework Integrating Physical, Control, and Cognitive Layers Author: Dr. Siamak Noorolahi Affiliation: SBMU Abstract Traditional intelligent systems are built upon the classical von Neumann architecture, which relies on deterministic logic and linear hierarchical processing. This paradigm faces significant limitations when addressing high-dimensional, non-linear, and stochastic environments. This paper proposes a novel framework for Quantum Intelligent Systems (QIS) based on Hybrid Quantum Logic. We introduce a multi-layered architecture comprising the Physical Layer, the Control Layer, and the Cognitive Layer, interconnected through quantum phenomena such as superposition and entanglement. Unlike classical systems where layers are strictly sequential, our framework treats the system as a unified quantum field where information processing, actuation, and cognition occur through the controlled collapse of a system-wide wave function. This approach provides a theoretical basis for achieving unprecedented levels of autonomy and strategic adaptability in complex robotic and autonomous systems. Keywords: Quantum Intelligent Systems (QIS), Hybrid Quantum Logic, Cognitive Layer, Entanglement-based Control, Wave Function Collapse in Decision Making.
